_meta.indication: Treatment of carcinoid syndrome diarrhea in combination with somatostatin analog (SSA) therapy in adults inadequately controlled by SSA therapy.

pivotal_trials.design: A 12-week double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized, multicenter trial; patients randomized to placebo, Xermelo 250 mg three times daily, or Xermelo 500 mg three times daily.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with a well-differentiated metastatic neuroendocrine tumor and carcinoid syndrome diarrhea having between 4 to 12 daily bowel movements despite stable SSA therapy for at least 3 months.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: The change from baseline in the number of daily bowel movements averaged over the 12-week treatment period.
pivotal_trials.n: 90 patients evaluated for efficacy (45 Xermelo 250 mg TID, 45 placebo).
pivotal_trials.result: Xermelo 250 mg TID reduced bowel movements/day by -1.4 vs -0.6 for placebo; estimated treatment difference -0.8 (97.5% CL -1.3, -0.3), p<0.001.

nct_ctgov.title: TELESTAR (Telotristat Etiprate for Somatostatin Analogue Not Adequately Controlled Carcinoid Syndrome)

pivotal_trials.design: A double-blind, placebo-controlled multi-national trial with three arms: placebo, telotristat ethyl 250 mg (TID) and telotristat ethyl 500 mg (TID).
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Carcinoid Syndrome (CS): on a stable dose of SSA therapy and with <4 BMs/day and with >=1 sign/symptom of CS, OR not on SSA therapy and with >=1 sign/symptom of CS.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: % change from baseline in 24 hour u5-HIAA levels at Week 12.
pivotal_trials.result: The results of the primary analysis of Study LX303 (u5-HIAA) were confirmed but the reviewers concluded the results were difficult to interpret due to very high variability and observed baseline imbalance; the change in BM frequency (a secondary endpoint) could not be used to formally replicate the primary efficacy findings of Study LX301.

nct_ctgov.title: Telotristat Etiprate for Carcinoid Syndrome Therapy

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5% and greater than placebo) included nausea (13% vs 11%), headache (11% vs 4%), increased GGT (9% vs 0%), depression (9% vs 7%), and peripheral edema (7% vs 2%). Constipation is an identified risk requiring monitoring; in a 12-week placebo-controlled trial, 2 of 45 patients treated with a higher than recommended dosage of Xermelo reported constipation, and in one of these patients the constipation was serious, resulting in hospitalization.
target_moa: Telotristat, the active metabolite of the prodrug telotristat ethyl, inhibits tryptophan hydroxylase, the rate-limiting enzyme in serotonin biosynthesis, reducing serotonin production that mediates carcinoid syndrome diarrhea.
modality: Small molecule (oral tryptophan hydroxylase inhibitor; first-in-class new molecular entity).

rems.type: REMS (Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy) is not required.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting or other external consultations was held.
